title: Highlighting Water First on World Water Day
author: Emma
body:
In celebration of World Water Day, the APT Foundation is recognising the important work that our charity partner, Water First, undertakes in Indigenous communities across Canada.

World Water Day has been celebrated on the 22 of March since 1993. It highlights the importance of accessible drinking water and sustainable management of freshwater resources.

In numerous Indigenous communities across Canada, tap water is not safe to drink. The water challenges faced by many Indigenous communities in Canada are complex. Some communities are concerned about infrastructure, whereas some do not have the capacity to train people in operating and maintaining systems to ensure safe, clean water. Safe water needs skilled people.

In January, the APT Foundation donated $5,000 to Water First, which in turn the APT Foundation’s donations provided Indigenous communities with the opportunity to participate in Water First’s Drinking Water Internship Program. The program supports young Indigenous adults to become certified water treatment plant operators in 15 months. With over 50,000 hours of hands-on training in water treatment plants to date, the long term affects within Indigenous communities are changing lives.


We are proud to continue donating to Water First. If you’d like to learn more about the charity and their ongoing work, please visit their website here.
